# Subject: Project LENS Sprint Sync | 09/28/2026

Date: 09/28/2026
Time: 05:02 PM - 05:12 PM ET (Duration: ~10m)
Attendees:
- Cameron Mercer (PartnerAdvisory, Lead Systems Engineer)

# Meeting Objective & Operational Context
The sprint team convened to review and finalize the persistent SQLite knowledge graph concurrency model. To support multi-threaded batch ingestion waves alongside concurrent real-time query services without operational deadlocks, the platform requires rigorous serialized writes, WAL journaling, and fail-closed busy timeout parameters.

# Key Discussion Points, Concurrency Spikes & Database Performance
Cameron Mercer presented empirical stress testing results evaluating SQLite concurrency across 16 parallel workers. The previous default rollback journal exhibited frequent lock contention during multi-stage ingestion waves. Transitioning to WAL mode with normalized busy handlers completely eliminated database lock failures while maintaining high read throughput.

# Strategic Synthesis
| # | What We Heard | What It Means |
| 1 | Rollback journaling creates uncoordinated write starvation | Persistent WAL journal mode and serialized queues are non-negotiable |

# Business Meaning and Value Case
Business Problem: Opaque database locking and uncoordinated writes risk pipeline crashes and corrupted graph state during mission-critical batch ingestions. Value at Stake: Eliminating ingestion restarts protects delivery deadlines and ensures immediate graph availability for decision intelligence services. Target: Zero lock starvation and 100% transaction atomicity under 16 concurrent workers. Value Mechanism: Governed DatabaseManager connection pooling enforces WAL mode, synchronous normal, and 30-second busy timeout handlers.

# Executive Decision & Architectural Commitments
Executive Conclusion: The engineering team formally ratifies the WAL-mode database architecture for all canonical graph storage. Decision Required: Ratification of WAL journal mode and serialized write queue. Recommended Choice: Adopt WAL journal mode with 30s busy timeout and in-memory serialized journal. Decision Owner: Cameron Mercer. Decision Deadline: 09/29/2026. Consequence of Delay: Risk of database locks during production ingestion waves.

# Immediate Delivery Scope & Release Boundaries
Target User: Data pipeline engineers and background ingestion workers. In Scope for Delivery: Implementation of ConnectionPool with mandatory PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL, PRAGMA busy_timeout=30000, and PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL across storage services. Explicitly Out of Scope: Distributed multi-node clustering or migration to PostgreSQL. First Deliverable: Connection manager PR and 16-worker stress test suite. Acceptance Test: Stress test suite passes 1000 transactions without lock timeout.

# Next Steps & Action Items
| # | Action Item | Accountable Owner | Responsible Party | Target Timing | Transcript Locator |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | Validate WAL concurrency stress harness under 16 parallel workers | Cameron Mercer | PartnerAdvisory | 10/12/2026 | [05:20] |

# Open Decisions / Blockers
None. Engineering team is aligned on SQLite WAL architecture.

# Appendix: Detailed Stakeholder Perspectives & Contribution Breakdown

# Cameron Mercer - PartnerAdvisory, Lead Systems Engineer
- Technical Architecture Constraints: Cameron Mercer detailed the empirical concurrency benchmarks, emphasizing that uncoordinated SQLite writes inevitably trigger operational lock errors under concurrent worker load. He demonstrated that enabling WAL journal mode with synchronous normal and an in-memory write serializer prevents read-write contention.
- Operational Implementation Plan: Stefan confirmed that all database access must route strictly through the governed DatabaseManager connection factory. He committed to delivering the 16-worker concurrency stress test harness and verifying clean lock acquisition before main promotion.
